articles.headline: Discord is cutting memory usage and speeding up boot times - joins Xbox, Epic, Steam, and more for similar upgrades just this year
keyFacts: Discord is switching its client from Electron to Rust to reduce memory usage and improve boot times, according to CTO Stanislav Vishnevskiy.
Vishnevskiy demonstrated the updated client running on approximately 290 MB of memory and opening significantly faster than the current version.
Vishnevskiy stated that the new client will enter testing with users soon, though no official release date has been announced.
body: Open up Task Manager and check how much memory Discord is currently hogging on your PC. If it's anything like mine, it's probably north of 500 MB. Alas, things should change soon, as Discord is moving the client completely over to a new programming language. It might not sound like that big of a deal, but Discord's CTO, Stanislav Vishnevskiy, shows it running on as little as 290 MB of memory.

Discord is switching from Electron to Rust. Electron is a software framework, a building block that allows JavaScript apps (among others) to run standalone on desktops. Built on Chromium, the underlying model behind Google Chrome, there is an overhead here that swapping to Rust aims to fix.

Vishnevskiy says, "We've been early adopters of Rust since 2018 and a lot of our infra, voice tech, and even some of the current client is already Rust, the holy grail was getting the whole client there. That means Electron goes away, and so does React Native, mobile keeps native UI but shares app code with desktop via Rust."

Though some suspected Discord would be swapping to Rust using Tauri (an open-source framework for desktop and mobile platforms), Vishnevskiy says it's actually using GPUI (a framework written in Rust), but "We have our own patches on top of it".

Vishnevskiy also says the goal is to get the program into testing with users soon, but no official date has been given. Either way, with Vishnevskiy showing off a resource demand of 290.2 MB whilst active, that's still a pretty big dip below what it runs at now. Mine is currently flitting between 500 and 600 MB, and my colleague Jacob saw it go up to 785 MB running on Windows.

Reportedly, the new Discord client is also faster to use, booting much quicker. Vishnevskiy showed two laptops, one with the old client and one with the new, and the new client opens up significantly faster (six seconds versus one in my approximation).

Naturally, we are hearing this from the mouth of the company, so we'll have to get the new Discord client in our hands to see how much faster and how much more efficient it really is, but anyway, to get a little more out of your current memory will always be a boon right now.
The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products
The memory crisis is continuing to drive the prices of gaming gear up, but software tweaks like this (including both Epic and Steam getting faster) are very much welcome in my eyes.

James is a more recent PC gaming convert, often admiring graphics cards, cases, and motherboards from afar. It was not until 2019, after just finishing a degree in law and media, that they decided to throw out the last few years of education, build their PC, and start writing about gaming instead. In that time, he has covered the latest doodads, contraptions, and gismos, and loved every second of it. Hey, it’s better than writing case briefs.

articles.headline: Luka Doncic's remarkable scoring streak gives Lakers a new challenge
keyFacts: Luka Doncic enters Friday's game against Portland averaging an NBA-leading 38.5 points per game and has scored at least 40 points in three consecutive games.
Doncic has recorded six straight games with at least 35 points, five rebounds, five assists, and five made three-pointers.
The Lakers will host Portland on Friday attempting to extend their winning streak and avenge a previous 136-129 loss to the Trail Blazers on Oct. 27.
body: Luka Doncic has been producing extraordinary numbers for the Los Angeles Lakers, and Friday's game against Portland offers another opportunity to extend one of the NBA's most impressive early-season streaks.

Doncic has scored at least 40 points in three consecutive games, averaging 42.3 during that stretch. The Lakers have won all three contests, demonstrating how effectively their superstar's offensive production has translated into team success.
But the scoring totals tell only part of the story.
Doncic is producing more than points

Doncic has recorded six straight games with at least 35 points, five rebounds, five assists and five made three-pointers. That combination highlights the versatility that makes him one of the league's most difficult players to defend.

Opponents must account for his scoring from beyond the arc while also protecting against his ability to create opportunities for teammates. Doncic enters Friday averaging an NBA-leading 38.5 points per game.

His recent performances have helped Los Angeles overcome difficult opponents and establish momentum after an uneven start. The Lakers will attempt to extend their winning streak to four games when they host Portland.
Trail Blazers have their own momentum

Portland enters the game with three consecutive wins, including a 132-119 decision over Phoenix. Damian Lillard scored 25 points against the Suns and has provided important offensive production since returning from an Achilles injury that cost him the previous season.

The Trail Blazers have also received contributions from Donovan Clingan and Deni Avdija. Portland has been navigating injury challenges, including the absence of Ja Morant and a fractured ankle suffered by Vit Krejci.
Despite those setbacks, the Trail Blazers have continued finding ways to win. They also defeated Los Angeles 136-129 on Oct. 27, giving the Lakers additional motivation entering Friday.

Lakers need their superstar to stay hot

Doncic's recent scoring streak has been remarkable, but Los Angeles will need more than one player to defeat a Portland team that has already beaten it this season. The Lakers must also improve defensively after allowing 136 points in their previous meeting.
That challenge becomes particularly important against a Trail Blazers team capable of generating offense from several positions.
Doncic's ability to create difficult shots gives Los Angeles an advantage in close games. However, maintaining the winning streak will require dependable production throughout the lineup.
Friday provides another opportunity for Doncic to extend his extraordinary individual run while helping the Lakers continue climbing the Western Conference standings.

articles.headline: Texas A&M volleyball's middle blockers lead SEC in two categories
keyFacts: Texas A&M volleyball middle blockers Eliza Sharp and Kaia Castle lead the SEC in separate blocking categories.
Sharp averages 1.36 blocks per set in all matches, while Castle averages 1.36 blocks per set in conference play.
The 14-9 Aggies play a road match against Vanderbilt on Friday as they approach the NCAA Tournament.
body: No. 17 Texas A&M volleyball has developed one of the SEC's most productive defensive combinations in the middle, with Eliza Sharp and Kaia Castle providing a consistent presence at the net.

The Aggies highlighted the duo's production Tuesday on social media, recognizing both middle blockers for leading the conference in separate statistical categories. According to the team's graphic, Sharp averages 1.36 blocks per set across all matches, ranking first in the SEC. Castle also averages 1.36 blocks per set against conference opponents, giving Texas A&M the league leader in SEC-only play.

The recognition comes after Castle earned SEC Defensive Player of the Week honors following two strong performances against ranked opponents. The junior recorded a season-high 12 blocks in Texas A&M's four-set victory over No. 6 Tennessee before adding five more in Sunday's three-set loss to No. 14 Texas.

Castle's performance against Tennessee was particularly impressive, as her 12 blocks ranked among the best four-set totals in program history. The Aggies finished the victory with a season-high 16 team blocks, helping secure another significant win over a top-10 opponent.

Sharp has also been instrumental in Texas A&M's defensive success. Her ability to disrupt opposing attacks has given head coach Jamie Morrison another dependable presence in the middle, complementing Castle's recent production.

The combination could become increasingly important as Texas A&M enters the final stretch of its SEC schedule. The Aggies are 14-9 overall and 7-4 in conference play, with another ranked road matchup awaiting Friday against Vanderbilt. With the NCAA Tournament approaching, Texas A&M's blocking ability remains one of its most valuable assets as the Aggies look to build momentum and improve their postseason positioning.

articles.headline: Former Rockstar Games tech director thinks GTA 6 could be coming to PC sooner than you'd expect to curb AI clones
keyFacts: Former Rockstar technical director Obbe Vermeij stated that generative AI could push Rockstar to release the PC version of GTA 6 sooner.
Vermeij warned that someone might use AI to convert the PS5 version to PC, potentially harming official sales.
Vermeij emphasized he does not know Rockstar's actual plans but believes AI tools are capable of such porting efforts.
body: Former Rockstar Games North technical director Obbe Vermeij believes that the possibility of AI vibe coded ports of Grand Theft Auto 6 could push Rockstar to create an official PC version sooner than you'd expect.

Speaking to RockPaperShotgun as part of a wider interview, Vermeij said generative AI "really has changed the world.". He elaborated: "I think I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC, which won't be as good as [the developer's] effort, but it could still also hurt their sales. So, I wouldn't be surprised if there was an effort to get [the releases] a little bit closer together."
Vermeij emphasised that he doesn't know what Rockstar's plans are, but with his technical expertise, he does believe that generative AI tools are "probably" capable of pulling off a GTA 6 PC port.

"It will take a long time. It actually, physically takes hours and hours and hours to do these things," Vermeij said. "And it will take a bunch of tokens and everything, so it would probably cost like, tens of thousands of dollars in tokens. But like, you know, if it's GTA, I think people are gonna try it.".

We've already seen people thrust footage of Grand Theft Auto 6 into AI software over the past few months. AI slop videos have been pulling in millions of views on social media, and people have been 'improving' trailer footage with Nvidia's DLSS5 'yassification' machine (thanks Ars Technica). Grand Theft Auto 6 itself will not feature any generative AI or microtransactions at launch.

AI game clones continue to be a problem. Game developers have cancelled public demos in fear of having their game copied, and Steam owner Valve has gone out to say it's the developer's responsibility to prevent cloning by making their games more original. Even as Anthropic has introduced measures to prevent such practices, other AI software can still perform such tasks.

articles.headline: Miami's timeline of transfer QBs: How Hurricanes transformed Darian Mensah, Carson Beck and Cam Ward
keyFacts: Miami head coach Mario Cristobal has successfully landed three consecutive high-profile transfer quarterbacks in Cam Ward, Carson Beck, and Darian Mensah.
Carson Beck led the Hurricanes to their first-ever national title game appearance since the 2001-02 season.
Darian Mensah transferred to Miami from Duke and has led the top-ranked Hurricanes to an undefeated start on the season.
body: Having an experienced starter at quarterback is key for any college football program to achieve success. One way to do just that is by getting signal-callers from the transfer portal. Perhaps the school that's been most successful in doing so is the No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes.

For the past three straight seasons, Canes head coach Mario Cristobal has landed three big-time transfer quarterbacks. His first was former Washington State signal-caller Cam Ward in 2024. Last season, he turned to former Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Carson Beck. He helped lead Miami to its first-ever national title game since the 2001-02 season.
2026 might be Cristobal's most effective transfer quarterback yet, as he landed Darian Mensah from Duke.
Let's run through a brief history of Miami's transfer portal quarterbacks, from Ward to Mensah.
2024: Miami lands Cam Ward from Washington State

Prior to going the transfer portal route, Miami had former Canes quarterback Tyler Van Dyke under center for three seasons. He had an up-and-down career, and Miami's best record with him was a 7-6 finish in 2023. He transferred to Wisconsin in December 2023.

In January, Cristobal landed former Washington State quarterback Cam Ward. Although Ward had previously declared for the 2024 NFL Draft, he did not hire an agent and was thus still eligible to play in college.
Across his two seasons at Wazzu, he threw for 6,968 yards with 48 touchdowns and 16 interceptions, rushing for another 13 scores on the ground.
Ward did not receive an FBS offer coming out of high school in West Columbia, Texas. He started his career at FCS Incarnate Word from 2020-2021.

At Miami, Ward had one of the best seasons of his career. He threw for 4,313 yards with 39 touchdowns and seven interceptions, rushing for 204 yards and four scores. The Canes finished with their best record under Cristobal at 10-3, but regular-season losses to Georgia Tech and Syracuse kept Miami out of the CFP.
2025: Carson Beck transfers to Miami from Georgia

Carson Beck was at Georgia from 2020-2024. He started his career as a backup to Stetson Bennett from 2020-2022 and was named Georgia's starter ahead of the 2023 season. He led Georgia to a 10-1 season that year, throwing for a career-high 3,941 yards with 24 touchdowns and six interceptions. The Bulldogs lost to Alabama 27-24 in the SEC Championship, but beat Florida State 63-3 in the Orange Bowl.

In 2024, he had another strong year at Georgia, throwing for 3,485 yards with 28 touchdowns. But he did take 18 sacks, along with fumbling five times and throwing 12 interceptions. That season, during Georgia's SEC Championship Game against Texas, Beck left the game with a shoulder injury before halftime after taking a sack.

He did not return to the game and was ruled out for the season with a UCL injury that required surgery. He finished 24-3 as a starter for the Dawgs. Although, like Ward, Beck himself briefly declared for the NFL Draft, he ultimately transferred to Miami in January 2025.

With the Canes, Beck led Miami to its first-ever CFP berth in school history, beating the likes of Texas A&M on the road, Ohio State and Ole Miss in the first three rounds. In the national title game, Miami fell just short against Indiana, losing 27-21. Beck threw for 3,813 yards with a career-high 30 touchdowns and 12 interceptions.
2026: Darian Mensah goes from Duke to Miami

Mensah might be Miami's best transfer portal quarterback yet. He has thrown for 2,425 yards with 25 touchdowns and 1 interception on the season. Miami is undefeated on the season so far, and ranked first in the nation.

He arrived at Miami after starting his career at Tulane in 2024 and Duke in 2025. He helped lead the Green Wave to an AAC title game two seasons ago, throwing for 2,723 yards with 22 touchdowns and six interceptions. He transferred to Duke ahead of the 2025 season, where he threw for another 3,973 yards with 34 touchdowns and six interceptions. The Blue Devils won their first outright ACC title since 1962.

He transferred to Miami ahead of the 2025 season, and is a Heisman Trophy candidate more than halfway through the season. Although his favorite target, Miami leading receiver Malachi Toney, is out for the rest of the regular season, the Canes are expected to make the CFP this season.

articles.headline: Kidnapped Teenager Rescued After Reaching Out For Help In Among Us
keyFacts: A missing Utah teenager was rescued from an Oregon home after being held captive for 18 months by Adam Hunter Harmel.
The victim used the online game Among Us on a Wi-Fi-connected phone to contact another player for help, leading authorities to her location.
Harmel was arrested during a traffic stop and officially charged in an Idaho federal court.
body: A 17-year-old Utah teenager was rescued by authorities in Oregon last month after being held captive for almost 18 months by 39-year-old Adam Hunter Harmel. The FBIâs 521-day-long search finally came to a close thanks to a chance online meeting in Among Us, after the missing teen used the game to contact a fellow player for help.

As reported by Newsweek, the missing teenager was kidnapped by Harmel in May 2025. The predator supposedly lured the then 15-year-old victim into a meeting via Snapchat, at which point he disposed of their phone and kept her captive in his basement for over 500 days.

More recently, Harmel gave the victim a new phone without cellular data. However, the teenager was able to connect to Wi-Fi via the phone and used it to access the online game Among Us. The victim then seemingly used Among Usâ in-game chat function to contact another teenager in a lobby. The two exchanged social media details.

From here, the victim explained the details of her kidnapping and, according to Newsweekâs report, stated that âshe believed police had stopped looking for her.â The victimâs contact relayed this information to the teen’s mother, who ultimately contacted the FBI. Authorities then set up a video call with the kidnapped teenager, during which the victim recounted Harmelâs abuse during the 18 months she was held in captivity.

The FBI located the victim at Harmelâs residence in Oregon on November 1 and discovered multiple pieces of evidence that corroborated the kidnapped teenagerâs account, including a knife that Harmel reportedly used to threaten the victim.

Harmel was subsequently arrested during a traffic stop in Ontario, Oregon, after the 17-year-old victim was found in his home. Harmel was officially charged during a brief, 10-minute appearance at the U.S. District Courthouse in Boise, Idaho, on November 4.

articles.headline: Two-year ban for 'Clicky Ponting' cricketer
keyFacts: Amateur cricketer Brian Devine received a two-year ban until September 2028 for clicking his fingers to fake a caught-behind edge.
The North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League sanctioned Devine and Saltburn second XI after investigating viral match footage and complaints.
Saltburn second XI was relegated to Division Three with a 60-point deduction and fined 300 pounds following the scandal.
body: - Published
An amateur cricketer has been banned for two years for his role in the 'Clicky Ponting' cheating scandal that made headlines across the globe.
Brian Devine, fielding at slip, clicked his fingers to mimic the noise of the ball taking the edge of the bat.
Devine, playing for Saltburn second XI, was filmed in a North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League (NYSD) Division Two match against Norton in July.
He has now been banned from all cricket under the jurisdiction of the England and Wales Cricket Board until 29 September 2028.
Saltburn's second XI have also been relegated from Division Two and will start the 2027 season in Division Three with a 60-point deduction. The club has been fined Â£300.
In a statement, the NYSD confirmed it has received complaints relating to the conduct of Devine and Saltburn in multiple matches.
Both the player and the club admitted the charges. Devine accepted his punishment, while Saltburn appealed against theirs.
Although Devine was the only player sanctioned, the NYSD was of the belief that other members of the Saltburn team were involved.

"In late July, the League received complaints about the alleged conduct of a Saltburn CC second XI player in NYSD Division Two matches and commenced an investigation with the co-operation of Saltburn CC," said the statement.
"The investigation ran over several weeks and included player interviews, written statements and a detailed review of video footage."

In footage of the game between Saltburn and Norton, Devine appears to click his fingers as the ball passes Noman Shabir's bat before being caught by wicketkeeper Josh Bowes. Saltburn appeal and the umpire gives Shabir out.
The clip went viral on social media, attracting media attention across the world.
Now, following the investigation and disciplinary process, Devine is not permitted to play, coach, umpire, score or manage junior teams for the duration of his two-year ban.
The relegation of Saltburn's second XI from Division Two means a reprieve for Middlesbrough's second XI after they finished 11th in the 12-team league.
Saltburn's first XI had already been relegated from the NYSD Premier League following their 11th-place finish.

"The League recognises the strain this has placed on many people, especially those who were abused online and in person," added the NYSD. "We ask everyone to respect that the formal process is now complete."
BBC Sport has contacted Saltburn CC and Devine for comment.

articles.headline: 25 Years Later, Buffy's Riskiest Episode Is Still a Brilliant Masterpiece That Changed the Show Forever
keyFacts: Buffy the Vampire Slayer aired its musical episode, "Once More, With Feeling," on November 6, 2001.
Actor James Marsters said the cast initially panicked upon receiving a cassette tape of creator Joss Whedon singing the songs.
The cast hired private coaches and rehearsed extensively before seeing a rough cut that convinced them the episode would succeed.
body: On Nov. 6, 2001, Buffy the Vampire Slayer made TV history. Again. The Emmy-winning series was already deep into its seven-season run when creator Joss Whedon came up with perhaps his most ambitious idea yet: a musical episode. The result was Buffy season 6 episode 7, "Once More, With Feeling," which remains a high point for the show and a frequent contender for best episode ever among diehard fans.

“Once More, With Feeling” isn't just a great musical (although it is) or a great episode of Buffy (it's also that). The brilliance of this 50-minute spectacle is how it combines the two, using a demon's curse that forces everyone in the town of Sunnydale to sing and dance as if they were in a Broadway play to push the show's overarching plot forward in numerous ways.

The best example of this may be the relationship between Buffy (Sarah Michelle Gellar) and Spike (James Marsters). The two had already been engaging in a toxic will-they-won't-they relationship for one season, and Spike takes the opportunity to get some big emotions off his chest while channeling Billy Idol in one of the musical’s best songs. At the end of the episode, when the curse is lifted but the revealed emotions still remain, Buffy and Spike share their first real kiss. Spoiler alert: their relationship does not go well.

But we're not here to relitigate "Spuffy." We're here to celebrate "Once More, With Feeling." To do so, I called up Marsters to recount the tale behind Buffy's iconic musical, from the terrifying moment he first found out about it to the episode's legacy 25 years later. Below, Polygon presents the behind-the-scenes story of "Once More, With Feeling" in the words of its breakout star.
Getting started
You might think Joss Whedon would gather his cast to tell them they were about to make a musical. According to Marsters, he shared the news in a more abrupt way.

James Marsters: Instead of delivering the new script for the next episode, we were given a cassette tape with Joss singing the songs of the show and plunking them out on the piano. And whereas Joss is an enormously gifted writer and director and producer, as a singer he wasn't quite up to the material. As a piano player, he's fine, but it didn't sound like it was gonna work. It just sounded cheesy. I'm a punk rocker, and I was like, “What the F is this?”

I remember ripping the cassette tape out of the deck in my trailer and walking out into the bright sunshine and squinting and holding up this cassette tape, and everybody else was doing the same thing, opening their doors and just going, “What the fuck? Did you just listen to this? What's going on here?” It just set off this deep panic as we discovered that we were going to be asked to suddenly do a musical.
While a few of the cast members, including Marsters and Anthony Head (Giles) had professional singing experience, most did not.

Tony Head and I were both comfortable singing in public. I'd been singing in bars since I was 13. I was in a band, which I'm still in now, called Ghost of the Robot. Tony played Frank-N-Furter on the West End in Rocky Horror Picture Show. But the rest of the cast had a really good point, which is like, “I'm not a singer. You hired me to be a one-camera dramatic slash comedic actor, and that's what I do. And now you're gonna have me go out in front of tens of millions of people, maybe across the world, maybe a hundred million people, and do something that I'm not a professional at. You're gonna ruin my career.” That's actually not a bad point to make. I think Sarah asked to juggle chainsaws rather than have to sing — like that would be safer for her career.

So there's all this gnashing of teeth. And at some point, I think we all realized there was no way we were getting out of this. It was gonna happen no matter what we felt about it, which is a good thing. You don't wanna be asking actors all the time, “Are you comfortable doing this?” You don't want a TV show where the actors are in control. You want the producers and the writers to be in control if you want a good show.

Once the cast accepted their fate, they got to work and even brought in personal trainers to develop the skills they needed. However, it still took seeing an early cut of one sequence from the musical to win most of them over.

The reason why I'm so proud of us as a company, and why it is one of my favorite episodes, is that even though we were sure that we were going to go down in flames and all of our careers were over, even though we were sure that this show was going to get canceled very quickly after we tried this, we decided to go down swinging. We decided to try our best anyway, in the face of certain doom. People started hiring their own vocal coaches and their own dance instructors on their own dime. All these people were showing up to set. People were rehearsing and preparing in the middle of filming the previous episodes.

They knew we were freaking out. So the first thing they filmed was the Xander-Anya sequence, the dance and the song. They did a rough cut of that and showed it to us. And it was wonderful. It was amazing. We realized this thing actually was gonna be really good.
Spike's song

Marsters initially struggled to find a way to perform his big song, "Rest in Peace," but ultimately figured it out by taking some inspiration from an unlikely rock and roll icon. He also praises the song for expressing Spike's emotions at that point in the series in a way the character never would have been able to through normal written dialogue.

I didn't really know how to sing that song. So I started playing it on guitar, and I hit something in the way I was voicing the chords. It started working for me and I found my way in. I brought my guitar up to the production offices and I was like, “I found it! This is how we gotta do it,” and I started playing. The producers go, “That's amazing, James. That would be like if Nirvana did the song.” I was like, “Exactly!” And they said, “No, this is not Nirvana. This is like a Broadway rock song. So it's got to fit in. It is different from the other songs, but it's got to fit in that show.” And I was like, “F you guys. I'm gonna sing it that way anyway. Even if you're not gonna do the instrumentation, I'm gonna keep what I found.”

There's a lot of frustration pent up in Spike. Buffy has been kind of like, “Come here, get away from me. Come here, get away from me.” I have experienced that as a man, and I'm sure women experience the same thing. So I was like: Thank God I get to express it. How wonderful would it be to just break out in a song and say, "Babe, either take me or don't. You're just torturing me right now."

That's one of the many things that was genius about the idea. I heard long ago that for the best musicals, there comes a point in the dramatic story where the character wants to express something that words won't express. They need another tool to get there so they can tell the person what's really up. And song and dance are the only way to do it.

There's this lift in the story, in the character, in the emotion that happens when you break out into song. Joss knew that and he used that to get his characters to say things that they normally never would tell each other — secrets that people keep hidden from each other — and the chaos that can happen if that stuff is let out all in one day.
The legacy of "Once, More With Feeling"

So why does this one episode hold up so well? For Marsters, it's not just because the songs are great and the plot is exciting, it's because it speaks to the inspiring theme at the heart of Buffy the Vampire Slayer.

The musical episode is most people's favorite episode of the show, and I think that's because it is frankly one of the best episodes of television that I'm aware of. It risked more. There was more work put into it. There was more creativity put into that episode than almost any other episode that I have ever seen. And I think the risk is really part of it.

The theme of Buffy is: Don't give up. It's hard to be a human being. It hurts to be here. The world is very imperfect, but don't give up on yourself. Don't give up on the world. Find something to fight for. What you decide to fight for is up to you. It might be taking care of your mom. It might be marching in the streets. But find the thing that's important to you and do it and don't give up on it. For one episode, we spoiled Hollywood actors lived up to the theme of the show. And then, luckily and wonderfully, it didn't suck.

articles.headline: DeSantis seizes on Florida victories to make case for GOP comeback
keyFacts: Gov. Ron DeSantis pitched his record as a national Republican model after Florida resisted a nationwide Democratic wave.
Florida Republicans retained control of both legislative chambers, but key state victories occurred by narrower margins than in 2022.
Strategist Angie Wong said DeSantis is promoting Florida's results to support a 2028 presidential bid.
body: Gov. Ron DeSantis (R-FL) is seizing on Florida ‘s resistance to Tuesday’s Democratic wave to pitch his record as a model for a battered Republican Party, even as narrower GOP victories at home raise questions about the strength of that model.
As Democrats dominated statewide in traditional Republican strongholds, including Texas , South Carolina , Kansas , even Mississippi , they did not break through in Florida .
“The blue wave hit,” Florida Republican strategist Ford O’Connell told the Washington Examiner . “Florida didn’t flinch.”
In the aftermath, DeSantis has underscored his political playbook in the hope Republicans across the country can learn from its pages.

“Let’s just be clear about what happened last night: This is as close to an extinction-level event for Republicans in many parts of the country probably as we have seen in the last 100 years,” DeSantis told reporters during a press conference in Tallahassee on Wednesday. “Out of the 10 largest states in this union, only one state will have Republican control of their state, the state of Florida.”
DeSantis’s leadership has captured the attention of Republicans, including conservative commentator Meghan McCain , but also some Democrats, such as party stalwart James Carville .

“The big thing about DeSantis for me is when shit really goes down and I’m panicking — he is always a light in the storm,” McCain posted on X. “He is a beacon of calm and clarity which is truly lacking right now throughout the entire party.”

The big thing about DeSantis for me is when shit really goes down and I'm panicking – he is always a light in the storm. He is a beacon of calm and clarity which is truly lacking right now throughout the entire party. https://t.co/dp01AwwmmJ
— Meghan McCain (@MeghanMcCain) November 5, 2026

“The Republican winner last night was Ron DeSantis,” Carville added on his Politics War Room podcast. “But Ron DeSantis can say we did better in — you know, ‘We want to win? Look at what we did in Florida.’”
But Florida’s results were hardly the resounding victories Republicans enjoyed during the 2022 midterm re.
Gov.-elect Byron Donalds (R-FL) defeated Democrat David Jolly by just over 1 percentage point, compared with DeSantis’s nearly 20-point reelection victory four years earlier.

Sen. Ashley Moody (R-FL), whom DeSantis appointed in 2025 to replace Secretary of State Marco Rubio, defeated Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon by fewer than 3 points. Rubio won reelection in 2022 by more than 16 points.
Democrats also made significant gains in Florida’s state legislature, breaking the Republican supermajority in the state House, although the GOP retained control of both chambers.
The results have fueled skepticism that DeSantis’s approach offers a solution to the Republican Party’s national problems.

“DeSantis is not the GOP savior,” former Trump White House communications director Alyssa Farah posted on X. “We squandered the Latino vote with overly aggressive immigration enforcement tactics. The guy who oversaw Alligator Alcatraz is not the answer.”
DeSantis is not the GOP savior. We squandered the Latino vote with overly aggressive immigration enforcement tactics. The guy who oversaw Alligator Alcatraz is not the answer. https://t.co/8mo36hmARz
— Alyssa Farah Griffin (@Alyssafarah) November 5, 2026
Florida Republican strategist Angie Wong placed DeSantis’s reemergence in the context of his failed primary challenge to President Donald Trump in 2024.

“He’s been largely sidelined by the MAGA crowds, right? And this dates back to when he won the first time, he won his governor’s race and Susie Wiles was his senior adviser, and those two had a big blowout after they won,” Wong told the Washington Examiner . “It’s the perfect time for Ron DeSantis to come out, not only because he has been unscathed by the MAGA world, because he’s not part of it, but more importantly, we don’t have a leader right now.”
“But understand, this is all on the backs of him trying to run in 2028,” she continued. “If this was a Machiavellian move, he actually did a really good job.”

Ahead of the blue wave, DeSantis did what he could to help Republicans avert disaster by pushing the Florida state legislature to redraw its congressional map mid-decade. The move netted on paper four new GOP-leaning seats. But on election night, three of these seats stayed in Democratic control, while the last one remains too close to call.

“In 2024 Florida voters sent 20 Republicans and 8 Democrats to the US House,” the governor posted on X. “In April 2026, Florida enacted a revised map to unwind an unconstitutional racial gerrymander. Last night, Florida voters likely elected 20 Republicans and 8 Democrats to the US House. Had the old map been in effect, it would have been 18 Republicans and 10 Democrats.”

O’Connell, the strategist, emphasized that “Republicans held every one of their 20 House seats.”
“That’s not a loss — that’s a fortress,” he said.
For O’Connell, redistricting “locked in a new map through 2030,” with more seats poised to be in “play for Republicans in a presidential election year with conservative voters fired up.”
TRUMP HELPS FUEL DEMOCRATIC TALENT POOL POST-MIDTERM ELECTIONS
A second Florida source also defended the mid-decade redistricting, telling the Washington Examiner “that redistricting ended up being the most expensive mid-term election in Florida history.”
“Dems spent a lot of money,” that person said.

articles.headline: A Hormuz deal leaves Iran its uranium
keyFacts: President Donald Trump stated Iran cannot be allowed a nuclear weapon, even as U.S. negotiators focus on a Strait of Hormuz deal.
An Israeli security official said U.S.-Iran negotiations focus on the Strait of Hormuz without addressing Iran's nuclear or missile programs.
According to the International Atomic Energy Agency, Iran has 440.9 kilograms of 60% enriched uranium, enough for about nine bombs.
body: President Donald Trump said on Wednesday he’d fight the Iran war all over again. “Long term it’s the only answer,” he told reporters. “You can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon.” He’s right about that. Which is precisely why the deal his negotiators are working on should worry him even more than the midterm election results do.

Israel’s security establishment has briefed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Defense Minister Israel Katz, and the Israel Defense Forces’ chief of staff, Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir, on three ways this ends.

In one, the talks drag on, and the whole region keeps arming. In another, the war restarts with a massive strike on targets all over Iran. In the third, Washington and Tehran sign an agreement opening the Strait of Hormuz all the way, on Washington’s terms. Which would settle nothing about Iran’s nuclear program or its missiles.

“Right now the American negotiation with Iran is focused on one issue: the Strait of Hormuz,” an Israeli security official said this week. “It’s not clear how that negotiation serves Israel’s interests on the nuclear program and the missile project.” It isn’t clear how it serves America’s interests either.
Washington and Jerusalem opened this war with the strikes of Feb. 28 to keep a bomb out of Iran’s hands, and Trump affirmed that existential goal again yesterday.

Yes, a reopened strait likely brings gas prices down — and gas prices just cost his party both houses of Congress. I understand the pull. But a deal that opens the shipping lanes and stops there leaves Tehran holding the thing the war was meant to take away. In other words, all pain with no gain.

When the International Atomic Energy Agency last counted, Iran had 440.9 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60%. That’s a short technical step from weapons grade. On the usual estimate, it’s enough for about nine major bombs if Iran takes it the rest of the way. A Hormuz deal doesn’t touch a gram of it. The scenario to watch is the second sliding into the first.

Two sources close to Gulf governments told Reuters this week that further limited strikes on nuclear sites could give Washington a way to claim its objectives were met and call it a day. A few nights of strikes, a victory speech, then a shipping deal. Every box ticked except the uranium.

Tehran has read the election as a win and isn’t hiding it. “Americans said NO TO WAR,” wrote Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf, the parliament speaker who leads Iran’s negotiators, the morning after. Mojtaba Khamenei, in whose name the regime now speaks, warned against “even the slightest inclination towards submission.” Neither of those men sounds very much like he’s about to hand over the stockpile.
YES, JD VANCE: LOSING THE MIDTERMS WAS ‘WORTH IT’ TO PREVENT A NUCLEAR IRAN

The new Congress takes their seats on Jan. 3. Until then, Trump holds the cards in this war. A Hormuz deal can carry a nuclear clause: the 60% stock shipped out of Iran, or diluted under inspectors with real access to it.
Washington must make that the price of opening the strait before Jan. 3.

Uriel Zehavi is Managing Director of the Mitzpe Institute (mitzpe.org) and writes the Israel Brief (israelbrief.com), Sunday to Friday. He is the author of four books, most recently Rooted in Judea: Lives and Law in the Heart of Israel.

articles.headline: After printing 40,000 whistles, this is the 3D printer I’d buy
keyFacts: A Verge writer recommended the Bambu Lab P2S Combo printer after testing four different models over one year.
The testing included printing 40,000 whistles for ICE whistleblowers and logging over 6,700 total hours of print time.
Bambu announced it will offer free replacement gears for select printer components manufactured between May and July 2026.
body: I’ve been wanting to try 3D printing, people tell me. Which printer should I get?
After printing 40,000 whistles, this is the 3D printer I’d buy
One year later, the Bambu P2S Combo is the only 3D printer I can easily recommend.

I finally have a fairly easy answer: the Bambu Lab P2S Combo. The auto-loading, fully enclosed touchscreen printer is one of the very few I can recommend. It’s the only one I’d buy for myself. It’s on sale for $649 through December 1st, but I’d vouch for it even at its normal $749 price.

I’ve spent an entire year testing the P2S alongside several competitors, printing 40,000 whistles for ICE whistleblowers along the way. After racking up 6,770 hours of print time across four different printers, I’m sure of my recommendation.
Some people who know 3D printers will argue with me:
- Some will say you shouldn’t support Bambu because it’s profiting at the open-source community’s expense.
- Others will say you shouldn’t spend so much when a $369 Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo or a $509 Bambu P1S Combo can print just as well.
- Some will say you should save $100 or more by skipping multicolor “Combo” systems.
- Some may even say, “What about all the fancy new tool-changing printers you just wrote about, Sean? Won’t the leaked P3C make the P2S obsolete?”

But for the reasons I’ll explain below, the P2S Combo is my pick despite all of that. It’s durable, reliable, and simple to maintain and clean and forget about, even in ways my trusty Bambu P1P and the similar P1S lacked.

The P2S makes 3D printing easy. When I’m in the mood, I don’t even need to walk over to my printer half the time. I can fire it up from my phone or laptop, using Bambu’s app to send one of millions of ready-made models from the cloud. The automated material system (AMS) automatically loads one of the rolls of filament that I leave in its protected enclosure for months at at time without fear. It automatically calibrates, automatically prints, automatically winds the filament back up when it’s done.

I tell friends that no matter which printer you buy, you should buy a multi-material system “Combo” because manually loading and unloading filament is a chore; it means standing around a printer waiting for it to heat up and feeding plastic into a tube by hand. Automated filament systems can fix that. For me, it’s not about having lots of colors in a single print; it’s about knowing I can print something black, or white, or red, or my kid’s favorite sparkly purple without any further effort — because I loaded those colors weeks ago.

It is true that the $369 Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo also has automatic four-color filament feeding at a seemingly unbeatable price, and printed whistles and household items just as well as the P2S. I’ve spent 1,271 hours printing with the Centauri Carbon, and 939 hours with a Centauri Carbon 2, and they printed almost flawlessly right out of the box — no need to level a bed, no need to adjust belt tension, the printer calibrates itself.

But like other Bambu rivals, Elegoo doesn’t automatically load its filament from mostly airtight containers. I can’t leave rolls of filament in the printer for weeks or months when I’m not actively using them because they’ll quickly absorb moisture from the air, turn brittle, and jam up the printer’s tubes or nozzle.

Moisture is the primary reason I wouldn’t recommend an inexpensive Bambu A1 Combo to newcomers, either, or a Snapmaker U1, or any other attractive multicolor printer without sealed filament storage. The entire experience of using a 3D printer is friendlier when you don’t have to prep the printer before printing.

Even so, it’s pretty dang tempting to save $280 or more by going with the Elegoo. But over the course of the roughly 1,000 hours I tested the Carbon and Carbon 2 side by side with the Bambu P2S, the Elegoo printers broke down in ways that were more difficult to diagnose.

The original Carbon’s extruder had some feeding issues and I found a lot of black dust inside after taking it apart, seemingly from worn plastic gears. Just this week, my Carbon 2’s stopped working after its nozzle mysteriously crashed into the bed and it refused to auto-level itself (which would normally fix that issue). I had to take the bed apart and still couldn’t find anything wrong.
In the end, yanking and reseating four tiny fragile-and-yet-too-tight connectors inside the bed fixed that problem, but it’s not the kind of solution a consumer should have to do.

Anecdotally, my Bambu printers have led a comparatively charmed life: In 1,692 hours of printing with the P2S, I’ve had to swap out the nozzle twice, clean and relubricate the traversal rods and screws several times, wash the removable magnetic printing surfaces a bunch of times with water and dish soap, and clear several filament jams in the AMS. That’s about it.

P2S nozzle replacements are easier, too. When you jam today’s Elegoo printers, you’re going old-school, either by wrenching off a hot nozzle so you can clean or inexpensively replace it ($25 for eight nozzles) or by fishing out tiny wires and unscrewing two bolts to remove an entire $30 hotend (which includes the elements that heat the plastic) at once. With Bambu’s P2S, you can just yank off a gasket and open one spring clip to swap a whole new toolless hotend ($18) in less than a minute. It does help to have a pair of mini pliers to grab the nozzle, though.

The Elegoo printers also have noisy fans that stay active even when you’re not printing, unlike the Bambu, though the Centauri Carbon 2 does shut them off more quickly than the original. Both Elegoo and Bambu let you remotely monitor your prints from its built-in camera and capture timelapse videos, but Elegoo’s camera and lighting are crap quality by comparison.

If I’m being completely honest, Bambu’s own Bambu P1S Combo, at $509 on sale, is the closest competition for the $649 P2S Combo, and I had a hunch it might be my pick in the end. I upgraded my P1P with most of the P1S upgrades, and it’s been a reliable workhorse: nearly 3,000 hours of 3D printing so far.

But over the past year, I’ve gravitated towards the P2S more and more because of its easy-swap hotends, the built-in touchscreen where I easily manage prints and rolls of filament, and all kinds of little improvements that I find I actually care about:
- It has a built-in guide that helps me put the P2S’s magnetic build plate in the right place every time, saving me from failures I’ve had with the P1P.
- It’ll automatically detect if I forget to put the build plate back, too, which saved me once this past year.
- The nozzle wiper is better at removing ooze that might wind up in your print and the poop chute clogs less.
- You don’t need to leave the door or lid open when printing PLA because it has active ventilation.
- It’s easier to add a second AMS later for four more colors, or just a single fifth roll on an external spindle.
- The stainless steel linear rods are easier to clean.
- I can sweep debris right out of the enclosure because the floor is a smooth ramp.
- The camera’s better, and video from it is far better lit.
- The AMS 2 makes it far easier to clear bits of old brittle filament without taking the unit apart.

Plus, I did have to replace the entire heatbed on my P1P once. I can’t say that nothing will go wrong with the P2S, and you shouldn’t take away that they’re as simple as an inkjet. They will need occasional maintenance, you’ll need to load good-quality filament and probably want to avoid rolls that come on lightweight cardboard (I try to buy Bambu, Sunlu, or Elegoo refills for my reusable plastic Bambu spools), and even then there will be components that wear out.

After 1,600 hours, the AMS 2 that came with my Bambu P2S review unit sometimes complains when trying to unwind or rewind some rolls of filament from some slots, and I suspect it’s because some of the gears are wearing prematurely. Bambu recently announced it’ll replace some of those gears free of charge, but only ones manufactured between May and July 2026, and even then you’ll have to be pretty handy to install them yourself.

I strongly believe people buying their first printer should get something tried and true, fully baked, simple to use, and the P2S is the best yet. But even Bambu is still catering more to DIY enthusiasts who’ll tolerate the occasional hardware defect.
So yes, if you’re asking “Which printer should I get,” I think you’d be pleasantly surprised with a P2S! But I wouldn’t blame you for waiting a few more years.

articles.headline: Trump touts imminent decision on potential new attack on Iran
keyFacts: President Trump said he will decide soon whether to strike Iran or make a deal to end the war.
Trump spoke with Qatar's emir about diplomatic efforts to end the U.S.-Iran war, the emir's office said.
Energy experts told CBS News that U.S. gas prices could fall below four dollars a gallon by next week.
body: What to know about the Iran war today:
- President Trump said Thursday that the world "will know very soon" his decision on whether to make a deal to end the , or to order new strikes to "destroy what is left" of the country.

- Mr. Trump called the Emir of Qatar to discuss efforts to end the war, the Qatari leader's office said Friday. The exchange came as Iran's top diplomat held a series of calls with his counterparts across the Persian Gulf - part of "efforts to maintain stability in the region."

- Motorists could soon a gallon for the first time since July, energy experts tell CBS News. Global oil prices have ticked back up slightly after plummeting this week on expectations that the U.S. could increase pressure on Mr. Trump to strike a deal with Iran.
Trump holds a phone call with Qatar's emir, a key mediator in negotiations with Iran

President Trump called Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani to discuss efforts to end the U.S.-Iran war, the emir's office said Friday, amid a diplomatic push to avoid a new round of major hostilities.

Their discussion, which the White House had not provided any information about by Friday morning, came as Iran's top diplomat made his own calls Thursday to counterparts across the Persian Gulf aimed at maintaining "stability in the region" amid concerns in many Gulf capitals that Mr. Trump will order major new U.S. strikes.

Al Thani received a call from Mr. Trump, according to a statement from the emir's office, during which the pair discussed "the latest regional developments, particularly diplomatic efforts aimed at de-escalating tensions in the region."
The emir "emphasized the importance of continuing dialogue and relying on diplomatic means to settle disputes and prevent further escalation," the statement said.
CBS/AFP
U.S. gas prices could soon dip below $4 a gallon. Why are fuel costs falling?
Motorists could soon see U.S. gas prices drop below $4 a gallon for the first time since July, according to energy experts.

Patrick De Haan, a petroleum analyst at price-tracking firm GasBuddy, told CBS News he expected the national average for gas, which the price-tracking firm put at $4.06 a gallon on Thursday and early Friday morning, to dip below the $4 threshold by next week. He also predicted diesel could fall below $6 a gallon by Thanksgiving.

Gas and diesel prices have both dropped over the last week, thanks largely to market expectations that the U.S. would underscore public dissatisfaction with the Iran war and pile pressure on the Trump administration to make a deal to end the conflict, De Haan said.
"Oil prices have been falling in the run-up to the election," he said. "My read is because there was optimism that after the midterms these problems would be addressed."
Saudi-led coalition intercepts 2 missiles launched by Houthis

The Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's government said Friday that air defense systems had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Iran-backed Houthi rebels at Najran, a major city in southwest Saudi Arabia.
"Debris fell as a result of the interception, and damage assessment is underway," the statement said.
Iran says 2 tankers hit mines, caught fire in and near Strait of Hormuz

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said in a statement carried by state media Friday that two oil tankers hit mines and caught fire in or near the Strait of Hormuz, a day after Tehran claimed five other tankers had met similar fates.

"Two violating oil tankers — one east of the Strait of Hormuz and the other within the Strait itself — that attempted to transit via an unauthorized route struck mines," the IRGC said in a statement, according to state news outlets.

"These two tankers had deactivated all their navigation and identification systems. Supported by the aggressive and terrorist U.S. military, they attempted to exit the Strait of Hormuz via an unauthorized path; however, upon striking mines, they caught fire and were immobilized," the statement said.
On Thursday, Iranian media reported that five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz in similar incidents.
There has been no confirmation of any of the incidents from maritime officials, and President Trump has accused Iran of making up such attacks to drive up global energy prices.

A U.K. naval agency said earlier this week, however, that despite repeated assurances from the U.S. that shipping lanes through the strait are open and safe, there were at least 30 attacks on commercial vessels in the region during October alone, a record high.

Since the war began with joint U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb. 28, Tehran has sought to control traffic through the strait, a key passage through which, before the war, about a fifth of global crude oil supplies would typically pass. In response, the U.S. imposed a blockade on Iranian ports.

The U.S. military has escorted tankers through the strait, which, along with other routes has helped bring shipments from the Gulf back up to or at least near to pre-war levels, but ships continue coming under attack.
CBS/AFP
Putin and Iran's security chief discuss building an oil pipeline from Russia to Iran

Russian President Vladimir Putin met Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei in Moscow Thursday to discuss strengthening ties between the two countries, including with the potential construction of a pipeline for Iran to import Russian gas.
Speaking with journalists after their meeting, Rezaei, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, called it "an extremely important exchange," according to the Iranian embassy in Moscow.
"During the meeting with Mr. Vladimir Putin, discussions were held regarding the construction of gas pipelines from Russia to Iran," Rezaei was quoted as saying by Iranian state TV.
He noted the aim was to enable Iran "to address its own gas shortages while also facilitating the sale of Russian gas to neighboring countries.
"Despite being a major producer, Iran has long suffered natural gas shortages, which have been exacerbated by the war with the United States and Israel.
During the most intense phase of the fighting, which lasted nearly 40 days, the U.S. and Israel struck key Iranian infrastructure including natural gas refineries, according to Tehran.
CBS/AFP
Trump touts imminent decision on whether he'll order strikes to "destroy what is left of" Iran
President Trump said Thursday that people will "know soon enough" his decision on whether to order a new round of U.S. strikes to "destroy what is left of" Iran.

"Now we will make a decision [on Iran]. Do we want to go further ... and ensure that this will never happen again?" Mr. Trump told reporters in the Oval Office, adding that he believed it would take Iran "25 years to rebuild the country" from the damage already inflicted during the war.
"I would prefer not to destroy what is left of the country, if possible, but I may have to do so. You will know very soon," he said.

The president kept the possibility of a major new U.S. assault on Iran on the table in the run-up to the midterm elections this week, but hadn't renewed the threat since his Republican party's dismal performance in the vote, which he acknowledged was, at least in part, a repudiation of the war.
Mr. Trump told the Financial Times newspaper on Tuesday evening, as U.S. ballots were counted, that he had no immediate plans to order new strikes on Iran.

articles.headline: Bryson DeChambeau bet on wrong $5bn start up and YouTuber will never realize potential on DP World Tour
keyFacts: LIV Golf collapsed after BC Partners chose not to invest $300 million in LIV 2.0, according to attorney Matthew Williams.
LIV Golf attorney Matthew Williams stated during a court hearing that debtors are toggling to a value-maximizing wind-down of their business.
Bryson DeChambeau is ineligible to join the PGA Tour due to a blanket ban and has reportedly been offered a place on the DP World Tour.
body: Bryson DeChambeau will sadly never become the golf superstar that he could have become.
The failed LIV star will also find it harder to take over the golf world if he’s forced to stoop down and join the hard-to-find DP World Tour .
Bryson DeChambeau’s golf career will never be the same after LIV collapsed Getty
Five years after it started as the great disruptor , LIV is toast.
The breakaway tournament collapsed when BC Partners chose not to invest $300 million in LIV 2.0.

“The debtors were ultimately unable to bring the key parties to a fully consensual arrangement that would have supported a financially viable LIV 2.0 league,” LIV Golf attorney Matthew Williams told a Unites States Bankruptcy Court judge during a Thursday hearing, which will lead to a new Chapter 11 bankruptcy plan being filed.
“As a result, the debtors are not currently proceeding with the LIV 2.0 plan. Instead, the debtors are toggling to a value-maximizing wind-down of their business.”
Sift through all the legal mumbo jumbo and this is all you need to know.
Rory McIlroy and Tiger Woods were 100 percent right.
LIV, Greg Norman , Jon Rahm , Sergio Garcia , Brooks Koepka , Dustin Johnson, DeChambeau and all those goofy team names — Crushers, Majesticks, Torque, Hyflyers — were historically wrong .
There will surely be a six-part streaming TV series one day on LIV, which started with gaudy fireworks and ended looking like an athletic version of the Fyre Festival.
A whopping $5 billion was wasted on the failure of LIV, which ultimately became a surreal combination of sports washing and second-rate golf.
Now, DeChambeau and others who foolishly thought they were too cool for the PGA Tour could be forced to fine-tune their majors swings on the DP Tour, which barely exists in America.
DeChambeau could be forced to play on the DP World Tour Getty
LIV picked up steam in Australia but fell flat in the USA AFP

DeChambeau — who boasts more than 3 million YouTube followers and has golfed with US President Donald Trump, NBA superstar Stephen Curry and Hollywood comedian Kevin Hart — is ineligible to join the PGA Tour due to a blanket ban that lasts for one year from the date of his last LIV appearance. He’s reportedly been offered a place on the DP Tour.
The biggest problem with LIV was America.
To truly succeed, it had to make it big in the big-money USA.

But with the NFL, NBA , MLB , NHL , college football , college basketball, soccer, WNBA , Formula One, Indy Car, NASCAR , MMA , paddle ball and lacrosse already soaking up the weeknights and weekends of hard-working Americans from Maine to California, who had the extra free time to devote to Johnson’s silly 4Aces?
“We’re at our best when the lights are brightest on the biggest stages,” the LIV team’s bio read.
“We play, prepare, and show up together because it’s always Primetime.”
Rory McIlroy wasn’t the biggest fan of LIV Golf and the breakaway players Getty
Dustin Johnson is ranked No. 274 in the world Getty
An artificial intelligence robot could have coughed up a better promo line than that.
“Our team delivered world-class individual and team competitions across five continents,” LIV CEO Scott O’Neil said in a statement.

“Built a global business, secured pathways to The Open and U.S. Open, earned Official World Golf Ranking points, engaged with stakeholders focused on the health and future of the game, created value in our teams, attracted premier sponsors, brought investors to the table around a next-generation business plan, and built a league capable of attracting both elite and rising talent from around the world.”
That’s not what the headstone of LIV will read.
It’ll be more like, ‘We blew $5 billion and then disappeared.’
DeChambeau, Rahm and Co. bet their golfing legacies on the wrong start up, and their wavering careers won’t ever be the same.
